philosophers isn’t decisive.  And I didn’t offer it as such. I think it has some evidentiary weight, especially considered alongside a philosophical analysis of the arguments themselves, which I offered, though of course not of a fully comprehensive sort. 
Regarding the “vision” thing, I think that the proper method of philosophizing involves something like what Rawls described as reflective equilibrium. We don’t simply follow the logic of certain theoretical commitments wherever they lead. Rather, we test those theoretical commitments against our considered moral convictions. (And we test our considered mortal convictions against our theoretical commitments). To me, if a purportedly libertarian philosophy wound up endorsing a form of social organization committed to hierarchy, exclusion, and intolerance, that would be at least some reason to reject that philosophy. Part of the reason I was attracted to libertarianism is that I had a pre-theoretical attraction to *liberty*. That attraction is part of the standard against which I judge various libertarian philosophies.

THE EVIDENCE™
HILLARY CLINTON WANTS TRUMP'S SUPPORTERS INVESTIGATED
When Political Opposition Becomes Grounds for Congressional Scrutiny, How Many Americans Are Potential Targets?

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best Selling Author
The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

Hillary Clinton has identified an extraordinarily broad category of Americans she believes could face congressional investigation following the November 3 midterm elections: President Donald Trump, his administration, his family, his supporters, and his allies. The statement raises a constitutional question that should concern Americans regardless of political affiliation. Since when did supporting an elected president become a reason to investigate someone?

During an October 28, 2026, appearance on Kara Swisher's podcast, Clinton predicted that a Democratic Congress would investigate Trump and people associated with him. Her remarks were not an isolated accusation directed at a particular official or an identifiable criminal offense. She included supporters and allies without specifying what conduct would warrant investigation. She also warned that the election would be only the beginning.

That distinction deserves examination. Congressional oversight of government officials is legitimate. Investigating suspected corruption, conflicts of interest, abuse of office, or violations of federal law is an essential function of government. Investigating private citizens because they supported the wrong political candidate is something entirely different.

EXHIBIT ONE — THE SCALE OF THE PROPOSED SCRUTINY

In the 2024 presidential election, Donald Trump received approximately 77.3 million votes, compared with Kamala Harris's 75 million. That represents roughly half of participating presidential voters, although considerably less than half of the entire American population. Millions of additional Americans may identify as Trump supporters without having voted for him, but their number cannot be established from election returns.

Consequently, describing Clinton's statement as a demand to investigate more than half of the entire U.S. population would exceed the available evidence. The potential political constituency implicated by her language is nevertheless enormous. Tens of millions of Americans voted for Trump, and her undefined references to supporters and allies could encompass people far beyond his administration.

What constitutes an ally? A campaign contributor? A volunteer? A business owner displaying a Trump sign? A commentator defending administration policies? Someone who attends a political rally? Clinton offered no limiting definition in the quoted remarks.

Without that distinction, the boundary between investigating misconduct and scrutinizing political association becomes dangerously uncertain.

EXHIBIT TWO — THE CONSTITUTIONAL QUESTION

The First Amendment protects political speech, assembly, and association. Americans possess the right to support candidates, contribute to lawful political campaigns, organize opposition, and criticize elected officials without government retaliation.

The Fourth Amendment provides additional protections against unreasonable government searches and seizures, while the Fifth Amendment establishes important safeguards against deprivation of liberty without due process.

None of these protections makes a political supporter immune from investigation for suspected wrongdoing. But neither does political allegiance, standing alone, establish wrongdoing.

The standard must remain individual conduct supported by legitimate investigative purposes, not membership in a politically unpopular constituency.

EXHIBIT THREE — THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN OVERSIGHT AND RETALIATION

Congress has substantial authority to examine executive-branch conduct and investigate matters connected to its legislative responsibilities. A Democratic majority would be entitled to exercise that authority, just as Republican majorities have exercised it.

But congressional investigative authority is not unlimited. It cannot legitimately become a mechanism for punishing citizens merely because of their political beliefs.

Clinton's defenders can reasonably argue that she was describing investigations into specific people involved in potential misconduct rather than every Trump voter. That interpretation is possible, and her remarks do not establish a concrete plan to investigate 77 million Americans.

The difficulty is that Clinton did not identify particular offenses, distinguish officials from ordinary voters, or explain which supporters she believed warranted investigation.

For a former secretary of state and presidential nominee, that omission is consequential.

EXHIBIT FOUR — THE SUPREME COURT HAS ALREADY ADDRESSED THIS DANGER

In Watkins v. United States (1957), the Supreme Court addressed congressional investigative authority during an era when Americans faced scrutiny over suspected Communist associations.

The Court recognized that Congress possesses broad investigative powers but cannot use them without a legitimate legislative purpose. It also recognized the danger of compelling citizens to disclose political beliefs and associations under threat of government authority.

The decision established that congressional investigations must respect constitutional freedoms and cannot be conducted merely to punish individuals or expose their private affairs.

The historical parallel deserves attention. Americans should not have to fear congressional scrutiny because they supported Trump any more than earlier generations should have feared government retaliation for their political associations.

The constitutional principle does not change according to which party controls Congress.

EXHIBIT FIVE — THE POLITICAL PRECEDENT

Clinton's remarks also raise a practical question: What happens when the opposing party regains power?

If Democrats establish a precedent under which political supporters and allies become legitimate investigative targets without clearly identified misconduct, Republicans could invoke the same reasoning against Democratic supporters when political control changes.

Imagine congressional investigations targeting Americans merely because they supported Joe Biden, Kamala Harris, Hillary Clinton, or Democratic congressional candidates. Would Clinton defend that use of government power?

The question is not whether Trump or members of his administration should face accountability for unlawful conduct. They should, under the same legal standards applicable to everyone else.

The question is whether the definition of accountability can expand so far that political association itself becomes the basis for suspicion.

A constitutional republic cannot maintain that distinction selectively.

THE VERDICT — POLITICAL SUPPORT IS NOT PROBABLE CAUSE

Hillary Clinton did not explicitly demand investigations of every Trump voter, and claiming otherwise would misrepresent the available evidence. But she did publicly include Trump's supporters and allies among those she anticipated a Democratic Congress would investigate, without identifying the conduct that would justify examining those groups.

That is the troubling part of her statement.

Seventy-seven million Americans voted for Trump in 2024. Their votes do not confer immunity from the law, but neither do they constitute evidence of misconduct. Supporting a president, attending a rally, making a lawful campaign contribution, or defending an administration's policies cannot independently justify government retaliation.

Congress has an obligation to investigate legitimate wrongdoing. It has no comparable authority to treat political disagreement as an offense.

Clinton should clarify precisely which supporters she believes should be investigated, what conduct warrants scrutiny, and what constitutional limits she would impose on those investigations.

Until those distinctions are established, her sweeping language warrants serious criticism.

The United States is supposed to investigate misconduct, not political allegiance. The moment government loses that distinction, political accountability begins to resemble political intimidation.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

I went back to West Texas for my high school reunion last weekend, to a town called Canyon that I left when I was nineteen and have been away from for more than thirty four years. I abandoned that town, and I abandoned it because everything it had for me was temporary.

What I found at the reunion was not what I expected. Plenty of my classmates never moved away, but almost none of them actually stayed. They are in Amarillo now, in a different neighborhood in Amarillo, in a place in the region that makes them feel like they belong. A lot of the people who did not leave still left.

That distinction matters for anyone working on cities, because when we talk about economic development we are not really talking about big cities or even small towns. We are talking about neighborhoods, and we are talking about very specific places. If the connectedness has drifted up to the regional level, then a town can hold onto its family ties and its history and still fail to offer people a reason to be there.

The same question applies in South Florida. Are people connected to South Florida, or are they connected to Homestead and Miami Shores? It applies to Florida’s heartland too, where a town like Arcadia needs people living in it and loving it, not people parked in Punta Gorda or Port Charlotte who are merely close enough.

Belonging at that level is the work. It is the Main Street level and the CRA level, and it is where Gen Z talent, innovation and entrepreneurship actually land. It will not work regionally. Celebrating the headline relocations while ignoring what is happening on the ground is how a place ends up abandoned by the people who never left.

Stay paranoid.

Simon was a simple Galilean, a brother of Jesus, as the ancients called one's close relatives — aunts, uncles, first cousins; he was one of the Saviour's four first cousins, with James the Less, Jude and Joseph, all sons of Mary, the wife of Alpheus, or Cleophas, either name being a derivative of the Aramaic Chalphai. The latter was the brother of Saint Joseph, according to tradition. All the sons of this family were raised at Nazareth near the Holy Family. (See the Gospel of Saint Matthew 13:53-58.) Simon, Jude and James were called by Our Lord to be Apostles, pillars of His Church, and Joseph the Just was His loyal disciple.
.
Saint Simon the Zealot or the Zealous, was the name this Apostle bore among the twelve. He preached in Egypt, Mauritania (Spain), and Lybia, leaving behind him the fertile hills of Galilee, where he had been engaged in the healthful cultivation of the vineyards and olive gardens. He later rejoined his brother, Saint Jude, in Persia, where they labored and died together. At first they were respected by the king, for they had manifested power over two ferocious tigers who had terrorized the land. With the king, sixty thousand Persians became Christians, and churches rose over the ruins of the idolatrous temples.

" Beauseant at Montgisard 1177 "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
This painting places a Templar knight at the heart of one of the most improbable victories of the Crusades. On 25 November 1177, sixteen-year-old King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem already marked by leprosy rode out with a few hundred knights to stop Saladins Ayyubid army from reaching the Holy City. With him came Grand Master Eudes de Saint-Amand and roughly eighty Knights Templar from Gaza.

Contemporary estimates give the Christians perhaps 375450 knights and several thousand infantry against a far larger Muslim host that had been allowed to scatter while raiding. Saladin, confident the leper king would stay behind walls, was caught crossing broken ground near Montgisard (Tell Gezer / Mons Gisardi), between Ramla and Yibna. Baldwin knelt before a fragment of the True Cross, then ordered the charge. The Templars formed the spearhead. Their war banner, the Beauseant black above white, black to enemies, white to friends was the signal that no brother might quit the field while it still flew.

The shock of heavy cavalry smashed the unready Ayyubid line. Saladin himself barely escaped; most of his army did not.The scene you see is not a portrait of one named man but an emblem of that hour: white mantle and red cross pattee of the Temple, kite shield, the Beauseant replacing later anachronisms, stone churches of the Latin East rising behind the dust. It is offered so visitors may remember that history is not only catastrophe. Sometimes a small, disciplined force, a young king who would not hide, and a banner that meant we do not leave changed the map for a season.

Baldwins victory bought the Kingdom of Jerusalem nearly a decade. Saladin would return; Hattin and the fall of Jerusalem still lay ahead. Yet Montgisard remains the day the Temples black-and-white standard flew over a field that should have been lost.Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam.

text:
I really appreciate your response on this. I'd like to push back on there only being scant references to David's role as King-Priest.

Going all the way back to the beginning, Genesis shows that Adam is a King-Priest. Genesis 2:15: "The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it." The verbs in Hebrew are 'abad' and 'shamar', and they're the same words used for the activity of the Levitical Priests: Numbers 3:7–8, 1 Chronicles 23:32, Ezekiel 44:14. Eden was a sanctuary, because before the Fall God was present in the garden. Adam was a king because God gave him dominion over the earth and all creatures. 

Christians see the major conflict of the Bible as God rectifying the sin of Adam and Eve and restoring Mankind to filial relationship with Himself. The enemy of Mankind is the serpent, identified as Satan in the book of Job. To accomplish His plan, God calls Abraham and makes 3 promises that are made into covenants and fulfilled in successive stages (Genesis 12:1-3, I know I've been through this in other posts, but it's one of the keys to understanding the unfolding of Salvation history). 

1. A Nation ( Sinai Covenant)
2. National Kingdom (Davidic Covenant)
3. International Kingdom (New Covenant)

Jeremiah makes it clear that the New Covenant will not be like the Sinai Covenant: "Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the Lord." (Jeremiah 31:31-32). Jeremiah lived after the first two covenants had been established, so he could only have been talking about the 3rd covenantal promise to Abraham. 

You wrote: Similarly Zechariah 6 uses the name "צמח" a name explicitly associated the messiah see Jeremiah 23, 33. Now to be fair, there is a temporal read: this one is Zerubavel, Rashi himself offers both, but favors the temporal one. But my point still stands, I think Zechariah clearly meant both which is why he's using the language of Jeremiah to indicate this will be the case in messianic times as well.

I think it's fair to see a Messianic reading here along with the temporal, but I would say that the message is communicated in a way for the hearers to understand, not necessarily saying that the New Covenant will have distinct roles of Priest and King. For example, In Isaiah 66:18-21, a passage about the gathering of the nations, he says that God will select from the Gentiles priests and Levites: "And they will bring all your people, from all the nations, to my holy mountain in Jerusalem as an offering to the Lord—on horses, in chariots and wagons, and on mules and camels,” says the Lord. “They will bring them, as the Israelites bring their grain offerings, to the temple of the Lord in ceremonially clean vessels. And I will select some of them also to be priests and Levites,” says the Lord."

How could God make Gentiles into Levites when not even other tribes of Israel could be taken as Levites? I think the answer is that Isaiah was prophesying about the New Covenant while still using the familiar terms of the Sinai Covenant.

Ransomware remains a material business risk for New Jersey’s healthcare providers, public agencies, schools and private companies, according to national figures that offer the clearest available benchmark for the state.

The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center recorded 3,611 ransomware complaints in 2025, an increase from 3,156 in 2024. Reported ransomware losses reached $32.3 million, according to a McDonald Hopkins review of the FBI IC3 2025 Annual Report.

Those figures do not isolate incidents in New Jersey, so they should not be treated as a state-level attack count. They do, however, show the scale and direction of the broader threat environment in which New Jersey organizations operate.

More than 2,100 reported ransomware incidents during 2025 involved U.S. critical-infrastructure organizations. Government, healthcare, manufacturing and financial services were among the affected sectors. Each has a substantial presence in New Jersey, along with interconnected suppliers, software providers and professional-services firms.

text:
Latvia and Its Neighbors Asked for €500 Million to Defend Against Russian Drones. Brussels Said No — or Rather, Not What They Were Hoping For

Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia asked the European Commission for an extra €500 million to build a regional drone defense system, driven by fears of hybrid attacks from Russia. The defense ministers of all three countries signed a joint letter, and the Baltics were counting on getting the money as early as 2026.

Brussels, however, had other ideas. EU Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said there's almost no free money left in the EU budget — it's running out. Instead of non-repayable funding, the Baltic states were offered preferential loans under the SAFE program, which still has €21 billion left after the first call. Some costs could potentially be covered through the EU's Integrated Border Management Fund, but that funding falls far short of the €500 million requested.

Tellingly, Lithuania has already taken advantage of the mechanism on offer: last week its Finance Ministry submitted its first application for €1.06 billion under SAFE — for forming an army division, the Baltic Defense Line, air defense, ammunition, and equipment. SAFE is a temporary EU credit mechanism: unlike grants, the money has to be paid back. It's still unclear whether the three countries will submit a joint application for drone defense, or how much they hope to get.

text:
Oct. 28 Sts. Simon and St. Jude, Apostles by Father Francis Xavier Weninger, 1876)
.
St. Simon, whose festival the Catholic Church commemorates to-day, was surnamed the Cananaean or Canaanite, because he was born at Cana, a town in Galilee. In this town, Jesus wrought his first miracle, by changing water into wine, as is known from the Gospel. Nicephorus and some others are of opinion, that Simon was the bridegroom whose wedding our Lord and His holy Mother honored with their presence, but that he afterwards left his bride with her consent and followed Christ. St. Jude, the brother of Simon, is called Thaddseus to distinguish him from the other Jude or Judas' who betrayed and sold the Lord. According to Nicephorus, Mary Cleophas was their mother, and James the Less their brother. Other writers say that Simon and Jude were not brothers. The Gospel tells us that both Simon and Jude were chosen by Christ as Apostles; but when or under what circumstances this took place, is not recorded, nor have any particulars of their words and actions been left us. There is, however, not the slightest doubt that they, as all the others, constantly followed the Saviour, and although they forsook Him when He was taken prisoner, they had, after His resurrection the grace to see Him frequently, to be present at His Ascension, and to receive the Holy Ghost on Pentecost.
.
When, later, the Apostles separated to preach the Gospel, St. Simon went to Egypt and St. Jude to Mesopotamia. Both however, were also in other lands, to preach the word of Christ, and after thus spending 30 years in apostolic labors, they met again, by divine dispensation, in Persia. On their arrival in this land, they found the Persian army in the field; for the King had declared war against India, and was in the act of marching against it. Baradach, the general in chief, had offered many sacrifices to the gods, desiring to know the issue of the war; but no answer was given, which had always been given before, as the Evil spirits spoke through the idols. Hence Baradach, amazed at such unusual silence, sent to another idol which was kept in a place far from the camp, and desired to know the reason of it. Satan, answering through it, said, that the presence of two Apostles of the Lord Jesus Christ was the cause of the silence of the gods, as the power of these two Apostles was so great, that not one of the gods, until now so greatly honored, dared to appear before them. 
.
Baradach, having received this answer, had the two Apostles brought before him. He met them with great manifestations of respect and listened to them while they spoke to him of the nothingness of the gods which he worshipped. As he was desirous to know the issue of the war, they made use of the occasion to show him how false were the words of the idols and hence how groundless was the notion of their divinity. They bade him propose his questions to the idols, through the magicians as usual, and told him that they would give his gods permission to speak. The magicians were ordered to ask the gods, and returned with the answer, that the result would be a long, bloody, and disastrous war. The Apostles having heard this, said to Baradach: "Now, great prince, recognize the falsity and the deceit as well of your magicians as of your gods. A deputation of the Indians will arrive to-morrow, at this hour, in your camp, to request peace of you on whatever conditions you may choose to prescribe." Baradach, surprised at these words, awaited with great impatience the following day. At the very hour the Apostles had foretold, the Indian embassy came humbly begging for peace, which was forthwith concluded.
This event was reported to the king, who resided at Babylon. He called the Apostles into his presence, listened with great attention to their words, and after having been sufficiently instructed in Christianity, was baptized by his holy teachers. The example of the king was followed by the whole court and a great part of the city. After this, the holy men went through the other towns and villages of the kingdom, everywhere preaching the mysteries and truths of the Christian faith. Many thousands became converts, only the magicians and fortune-tellers remained in their blindness, and seeing, with deep resentment, that they were everywhere despised and derided, they sought means to kill the holy Apostles. To this end, they excited the inhabitants of a town, which was far distant from the residence of the king, against the Saints, who had no sooner arrived there than they were seized and dragged, the one before an idol of the sun, the other before that of the moon, and were commanded to offer incense. The holy men refused to comply with so wicked a demand, saying that they sacrificed only to the true God; after which they began to preach the Gospel. But the furious Pagans refused to listen to them, and in their rage, cut St. Simon asunder with a saw, and beheaded St. Jude. In this manner these two holy Apostles ended their lives and earned the glorious crown of martyrdom.
.
I cannot pass over in silence an event which took place while St. Simon and St. Jude preached the Gospel. The daughter of a noble Persian became the mother of a child, and said that a deacon of the Apostles was its father. The truth of this was not doubted, and the deacon was brought before the king. The holy Apostles, knowing that he was innocent, went to the king, and desired that the parents of the slanderer and the child should be summoned. When they appeared, one of the Saints asked the infant, in the presence of the king and the parents, whether the deacon was its father. The child answered loudly and distinctly: "No! the deacon is innocent." The king and all present thanked and praised the Almighty who had so miraculously saved His servant. The parents, begging pardon of the latter, as well as of the Apostles, requested that the child should be asked who was its father, but the Apostles said. " We come not to accuse the guilty, but to protect the innocent:" This great miracle was not only instrumental in increasing the esteem in which the holy Apostles were held, but was also the means of converting many heathens, and strengthening the faith of those who had already embraced Christianity.
.
It has further to be remarked that we have, in Holy Writ from the pen of St. Jude, a short but powerful Epistle, in which he admonishes the faithful to guard themselves against those who, having forsaken the true Church, preach heresy; to remain constant in their faith, and to practice diligently all virtues, especially charity, chastity and purity. Luther rejected this Epistle from Holy Writ, though St. Augustine had counted it among the inspired books more than a thousand years before, and also several Councils had declared it canonical. Without doubt Luther was actuated by the fact that he, and such as he, are painted with living colors in the same Epistle.
In the life of St. Bernard we find that this Saint had a particular devotion to St. Jude. He received, with extraordinary joy and veneration, the relics of this holy Apostle which were sent to him, and, on his death-bed, he requested that they should be laid on his breast and be buried with him.
.
PRACTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
.
I. More than thirty years did the holy Apostles work with unwearied zeal for the salvation of souls. Thousands of dangers, persecutions, nay, even death they did not fear, bearing everything joyfully, filled only with the thought of saving souls. What incited them to this? Doubtless, the love of Jesus Christ, who had ransomed those souls with His precious blood, and also pity, as they knew that, blinded by their error, these people would lose eternal life. St. Jude, in his epistle, exhorts us to have compassion on all those who are seduced by the heretics, and to save them from the fire, that is, from the fire of hell. "But others save, pulling them out of the fire; and on others have mercy." (Jude, xviii.) To-day I request you to have pity on your own soul. "Have pity on thy own soul," says the Wise Man. (Eccl., xxx.) Your soul has been bought with the priceless blood of Christ: esteem it accordingly, and take care that the blood of your Saviour may not have been shed for it in vain. Your soul, in its sin, is in the greatest danger of being cast into eternal fire. Have pity on it, and drag it forcibly from the precipice on which it stands. It is your soul, your own immortal soul, so dearly bought by Christ, given to you to guard and keep it. If you gain the life to come, your soul will be forever happy; but, if you lose it, your soul will eternally suffer in hell. Who will be injured by this but you? Therefore, commit nothing which may draw after it eternal punishment, and leave nothing undone which may aid you in obtaining the glories of heaven. It is your soul. "Have pity on your own soul!"
.
II. St. Simon is brought to the idol of the Sun, and St. Jude to that of the Moon, with the command to sacrifice; and, when both declare that they sacrifice only to the true God, both suffer martyrdom. Can you also say, with truth, that you sacrifice only to the true God? How many hours, how much labor, trouble and care have you sacrificed to vanity and pride, to the world, the flesh and the devil? Do you consider that less punishable than to offer a few grains of incense to a lifeless image? Oh! learn to despise this way of conducting yourself, and endeavor to live in such a manner that you may truthfully say that you offer sacrifice to the true God alone. Offer to the Almighty, early in the morning, all your thoughts, words and actions, all your cares and labors, and all that you may have to suffer during the day. During the day, offer to Him the incense which is most agreeable to Him,--that of prayer and good works. Offer Him your self-abnegation, the control of your evil inclinations, especially anger, impatience, and curiosity. Offer your self-conquest, by forgiving those who wrong you; by abstaining from unchaste and slanderous conversation; from intemperance in eating and drinking,--in one word, from everything displeasing to Him. Offer to Him, especially at night, a repentant and contrite heart, a heart ready to serve Him zealously and constantly." A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit; a contrite and humble heart, O God, thou wilt not despise" (Psalms, 1.). "It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity." (Eccl., xxxv.)

text:
People are free to visit monasteries, and even leave their parishes if they find better counsel elsewhere. This is not schism.

There are many tragedies at parishes, at no fault of the parish priest. The man you speak of was not a monk, but inquired and then left the monastery. They were not responsible for this tragic event.

The suspicions about “vast wealth” have been a slander since the founding of the monastery in Arizona when it was a few monks in a trailer in the middle of the desert. 

You can certainly find scandals regarding money in many jurisdictions in the US at the diocesan level, but the theory that an “enemy” paid “millions” to build monasteries for countless people to learn the teachings of the Holy Fathers, repent, and attend daily services is unhinged and divorced from reality. 

The abuses at parishes before Geronda Ephraim’s arrival would likely surprise even the most cynical today There is a parish that insisted on using a drum set and a guitar during Divine Liturgy, claiming it ‘could be Orthodox’, and continued even after a visit and reprimand from Bp. Basil Essey. Another, across the continent, had a priest remove all of the icons on the walls and replace them with mirrors, so the parishioners “could see the true saints.”

The problem has always been that people did not and do not like what he said, because this is largely a country drowning in a heretical protestant ethos. 

“We American bishops and priests, for seventy years, have wanted to attract people to the Church by holding festivals. That is, we held festivals and festivities, treating people to drinks, food, and entertainment. We forgot about prayer, confession, fasting, the rosary — all the things that make up the Tradition of our Church. We even discouraged the creation of monasteries because we thought they were unnecessary and had nothing to offer our Church. And then a tiny man, without worldly education or theological diplomas, without innovative and daring ideas (which we had in abundance), came and reminded us of the most important thing — our Orthodox Tradition. He did not call us to dancing and entertainment, but to fasting and participating in hours of vigil. And people responded to his call, came to the elder and supported him. The number of those who came to Father Ephraim is beyond description. America, which was seeking a way out of the dead end of the consumer culture and slavery to material values through various social movements (such as the hippies) and Eastern religions, discovered true unadulterated Christianity — Orthodoxy.” 

—Fr, Anthony Moschonas

text:
FIGHTING TO KEEP MY SERVICE DOG, STAR, AND MYSELF OFF THE STREETS 🐾❤️

Before my work injury, I did everything I could to rebuild my life. I moved to Wisconsin for a second chance. It wasn't easy starting over. I found a job but no real safety net or stability. I ended up back home in Arizona to try again. I keep trying. I am not asking for a handout, but I cannot do this alone anymore.
A severe work injury left me with debilitating neck, nerve, and lower-back damage. Coupled with a lifelong learning and mental disability, a heart valve condition, and intense daily pain, my doctor has ordered me off work indefinitely.

Now, the medical bills are piling up, we have lost our safe housing, and Star—my medical service dog, my protector, and my family—and I are fighting every single day to stay off the streets. Without a roof over our heads, neither of us is safe.

⛈️ Emergency: Flash Flood Risk & Severe Storms Looming Hours Away

The urgency of our situation is at a breaking point tonight. The National Weather Service has issued a Flash Flood Watch for metro Phoenix and most of Arizona, with back-to-back storms starting in just a few hours. 

• Friday Morning (Oct 30): The first massive storm wave hits with widespread heavy showers and thunderstorms. High temperatures will suddenly plummet to a raw, cold 68°F. 

• Saturday (Halloween): While daytime offers a partial break, a second wave of severe rain rapidly moves in during late night hours. [1, 2]

• Sunday (Nov 1): The storm intensifies into a massive continuous rain day with heavy downpours, a persistent flood risk, and temperatures stuck in the chilly 60s. 

Being unhoused or in temporary, exposed conditions during this drenching winter storm pattern is incredibly dangerous for my neck injuries, my heart condition, and for Star. We desperately need to secure safe shelter before the heavy morning downpours arrive.

Our Goal: $9,000 to secure safe housing, cover medical essentials, and stay together.

text:
Everyone's talking about the latest models and harnesses. But hardly anyone talks about the contracts that make the whole AI ecosystem work. Here are my insights and observations of how AI SaaS contracts (particularly at the B2B level) are being negotiated based on my experience as a tech lawyer who is deep in this work every day.

1) Structurally, AI SaaS contracts are not so different from traditional SaaS contracts. I'd say 80% of standard SaaS and commercial contracting issues (e.g. service levels, data protection, termination, warranties, etc) are carried over into AI contracts. There are obviously some nuances in AI that are very crucial particularly around agentic liability, training, tokens and outputs which I'll go into more detail below.

2) From a bargaining power perspective, it tends to start out as a vendor's market upon each product category release (e.g. LLM → chatbot → agentic harness) because of the lack of options. But as the market saturates with more options (and vendors vye for enterprise revenue), B2B customer gain more barganing power for a limited time window until the new product era kicks in which resets the balance in favour of vendor. This ebbs and flows every 2-3 years. Legal terms have become increasingly scrutinised as product differentiators because vendors know enterprise customers care about this stuff (e.g. see point 10).

3) I've seen instances where the vendors' standard legal terms are reasonable and pass Legal's checks, but then unload all the onerous terms / amendments into the order form / statement of work which are typically reviewed by non-legal product teams. I've seen so many 'traps' for example where the vendor offers a token discount but that is defeated by a take-or-pay minimum spend obligation, or insert new terms that override the standard terms.

4) There's always a fight as to how much the vendor can unilaterally change or amend terms. This is not a new issue, but SaaS agreements tend to defer key commercial terms on online product pages or clickwrap terms to which the vendor reserves rights to unilaterally amend. Customers have learnt to live with it by pushing for notificiations of adverse changes and the ability to exit if the change is too detrimental. But realistically, it's hard to just 'walk away' from a sticky solution, so customers typically end up having to monitor terms themselves and 'lock in' as many of the online terms into the enterprise paper contract (and give the enterprise contract the highest level of precedence).

5) On liability, in this agentic era, the core question is whether the agreement treats an agentic action as an "output" or a "service"? If the action is an output, then typically this is wrapped under output disclaimers (i.e customer is responsible for their own output). If the action is a service, vendors owe a standard of care with respect to their service, but this may be subject to carveouts (e.g. vendor not liable if customer misused the service, etc). Google is the only major vendor I've seen make an explicit statement that action = service. The other big AI vendors remain silent on this point, presumably to reserve flexibility.

6) By design, agents invoke tools (e.g. plugins and connectors). These tools are typically provided by third parties outside of the agent's provider.  Customers try to tactfully frame these third party tool providers as "subcontractors" or "subprocessors" of the vendor so that vendor takes responsibility for them. But almost always the vendor will reject that framing, disclaim responsibility, and defer the customer to the third party's terms of use. The result is that customer gets caught up a web of clickwrap third party terms that they cannot negotiate, which they then either have to accept or not invoke the tools at all (and build their own tools).

7) By design, agents are also 'consequential' in the everyday sense - i.e. they perform actions one after another in sequence, so one bad step can cascade through every step after it. The typical contracting principle is that neither party should be liable for consequential or indirect losses (i.e. losses that don't flow directly from the breach). However, there is a trend of customers tactfully trying to carveout agentic actions from the scope of consequential losses so that vendor remains liable for such actions. In my experience, customers succeed about 50/50, depending on how much the customer can rely on regulatory reasons that vendor can't push back.

8) AI training is a huge contentious battleground which cuts across IP and data protection issues. The standard 'acceptable' middleground is to allow the vendor to train their AI on anonymised / aggregated data, but not the customer's raw data. But as we increasingly see how easy it is to distil know-how and insights from anonymised data, many customers are getting nervous that their IP / know-how is still being exploited even if their privacy / confidentiality is respected.  So I'm seeing a reversal into "no training at all, even on anonymised / aggregated data" and ZDR (zero data retention, i.e. the vendor deletes your data once processed) clauses as the standard commercial position pushed by customers (though this often comes at the cost of a nerfed service).

9) In terms of IP, discussion tend to focus on the outputs - i.e. AI-generated content (e.g. images, videos, text) v AI-generated apps (e.g. vibe coded apps or workflows). For content, most agreements stay silent on who owns outputs, since many legal systems around the world still don't have a definitive position as to whether copyright subsists in AI generated content. Apps are different, and 2026 saw a boom in vibe coded apps. The portability of the vibecoded app typically dictates the IP position - i.e. "can you take your app outside of the environment?". If your app can only run on the platform, the vendor will say it's just a use of their platform and therefore 'part of the vendor's service' which is the vendor's IP (in which case the negotiation shifts to uptime, warranties and licence scope). On the other hand, if the app can be exported and run outside of the platform, the customer usually owns the IP in their app but also the risk that comes with it. The latter is becoming the mainstream now as we see agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) gaining more ground over no-code / low-code SaaS tools (e.g. Lovable, Replit).

10) IP indemnities (i.e. the vendor covers you if someone sues over the output) are an example of legal terms being flaunted to win competitive edge. In 2023, Adobe, Microsoft, Google and OpenAI offered comparable indemnity protections at their own risk in order to win more enterprise customers. I remember my clients asking me to compare those indemnnities all the time, so they do notice these things. But over time, other smaller players are offering the same so it's market standard now. The indemnities are also getting tighter since the volume of copyright lawsuits launched against the AI labs is making the industry rethink whether they can really absorb the indemnity costs.

11) Incidents such as the Fable 5 suspension in June 2026 was a wake-up call for enterprise customers (particularly those outside of the US) to lock down tighter service level agreements to ensure service continuity (especially since AI is getting more deeply integrated into business ops). Many vendors are willing to commit to onerous service levels (e.g. 99%) but the negotiation gets fierce in the carveouts. Vendors prefer to disclaim third party outages from their service levels and widen force majeure provisions so that they have more room to get away with in case they suffer an outage themselves (think of the Crowdstrike incident). Some vendors also try to make it hard for customer to track service levels and/or claim credits.

12) There's an interesting interplay between service levels and tokenomics too. If the vendor 'loses' on the service level negotiations, they could try to claw back leverage by tightening your rate limits or context windows which shrinks your usage, which in turn reduces the scope of service hours that the vendor has to promise. Because after all, how you will notice outages or service level failures when you've run out of tokens and can't use the service in the first place? The devil is thus in detail around token limits, reset windows, weekly caps, and whether those limits apply per user or are pooled across the whole company.

13) We're also seeing a tokenomics x consentnomics interplay. Anthropic has for a while offered discounted tokens in exchange for your permission to let Claude train on your raw chats. OpenAI has also offered complimentary tokens to API customers who opt in to sharing their data for training. That said, I'm not sure how sustainable this is because such programmes basically incentivise customers to only trade away their least valuable / low-quality data for token savings (which only erode profit margins for the labs).

text:
@LouStagner @Mike_kim714  sorry this'll probably be pretty long, but the context matters.... many moons ago I spent a few years researching this very question and started writing a book about the keys to High Performance Tournament Golf.

I live in Utah and was a member of Riverside Country Club where @BYUmgolf plays and many former tour pros are members and bring lots of other tour pros to come and play.

At the time "the journeyman" 😂 Dan Forsman was out with his son and invited me to join them.

For those who don't know, Dan kept his card every single year FOR 20 STRAIGHT YEARS!! From 1983 to 2003.

Won 5x on PGA Tour, played 652 Tour Events (made 422 cuts) and won 3x on Champions Tour - 242 Champions Tour Events (made 237 cuts) so if you're keeping score at home, that's 6 events shy of 900 FREAKING STARTS between PGA & Champs! 🤯

He's also one of the nicest, most thoughtful, easy going and genuine guys you'll ever meet!

So I was stoked at the invite and bit my tongue for as long as I could before I couldn't take it any more, ha! 😂

I've interviewed Billy Casper, 2 of his sons Bobby and Byron, Johnny Miller's son and BYU's head coach Todd Miller, Mike "Radar" Reid, Dean Wilson, Bobby Clampett, Danny Summerhays, Boyd Summerhays, Zac Blair, Tony & Gipper Finau, plus 10-15 former Korn Ferry players, probably 20 of the top players among the Utah Section PGA Professionals, and maybe 30 top amateurs in Utah of all ages, many of whom were professional at some point or another.

At the point I was playing with Dan - maybe 2006, I had interviewed quite a few already, so I was NOT gonna miss this chance.

After a few holes, I tell him about the research I'm doing and the book I'm working on and I asked him this question:

"you've seen every single 'can't miss kid,' 'generational talent,' '2nd coming off ____,' uber-hyped player to come out on tour for the last 25 years... what's the difference between the ones who 'really make it' and the ones who don't? Not just some hot flash in the pans for a few seasons, win a few and then vanish... But who really make it as pros?"

He asked me what others had said and I told him a few people's responses, he correctly guessed what some of his friends said, but then rather than agreeing/disagreeing with someone or just giving me an answer, he said..."let me think about it a bit."

We played maybe 5 more holes and only had 1 left - so I thought for sure he'd forgotten about it.

But he comes up to me says "OK Ken I've got my final answer! There are a lot of things you could say, but ultimately if I had to pick 1 thing it would be this...

If I've been playing with a guy for 2 days straight and he just hasn't had his game, he's been spraying it all over the place, lefts and rights, distance control has been sketchy, can't get the feel of the greens, and you can just tell for whatever reason, it's not their week... but we get down to the back 9 on Friday and they're 3 shots or more outside the cut line with no semblance of game, but somehow out of seemingly nowhere they find a way of getting the ball in the hole when they need it, making at least 3 birdies - that's important because anyone can birdie a par 5 coming in and get lucky hitting 1 other shot close enough to make a putt... but needing 3 or more birdies in 9 holes or less and finding a way of grinding it out when no one would bet on them to do so... THAT'S a guy I'm gonna expect really good things from for a long long time."

I thought that was brilliant, and so cool that he took so much time to think about it and give me his absolute best and " final answer!" 😂

text:
When I was 14, I started learning kanji and immediately complained about stroke order.

 context: Japanese uses adapted Chinese characters called kanji. Kids in Japan are taught to write each one in an exact stroke order, not just to make it look right.

"Why does it matter if it looks the same at the end?"

My mom was a math teacher, so she was used to me complaining about things like this and usually had an answer. She isn't Japanese, though, so this one stumped her.

I'd started Japanese at 11 but only knew hiragana and katakana. My public high school in Michigan offered Japanese, and I wanted to test into Japanese 2. To do that, I had to memorize 50 kanji by the end of the week. I had about two days. 40 would've gotten me a B, which was fine, but I wanted all 50.
So my mom stayed up with me until midnight with flashcards. I got 100% on Friday's test. Then it came time to actually learn to write them, and I froze.

I told her stroke order was stupid and a waste of time. "This is America. Surely we can do this more efficiently." She said I was on my own.

I tried everything to get around it. I drilled radicals on my own, looked for some cool calligraphy style to copy. Eventually I realized everything was just easier once I learned the stroke order.

This came up again recently! I was complaining to a friend who studied math at a high level that we're taught to memorize formulas without learning what math is actually doing. He said he felt the same way until grad school, when he realized you have to learn the formulas first because everything builds on them. I immediately thought of kanji. He's a native English speaker who learned Chinese characters for Mandarin, so he knew exactly what I meant.

It reminds me of what the neuroscientist Nikolai Bernstein called the degrees of freedom problem. Your body has too many possible ways to make any movement, so beginners lock most of them down. Once the movement becomes automatic, you can loosen up and get creative. I think rules like stroke order or memorized formulas do something similar for your mind: they narrow your options until the basics are automatic, and then you have room to actually think.

These days I barely handwrite kanji. Most of my Japanese is digital. But when I do write by hand, it's the kanji I learned back then, in the exact stroke order I learned at 14. A lot of processes seem inefficient or silly until you understand why they're there.

THE MERMAID AND THE CASTAWAY

Cinematic AI Video Generation Prompt

FORMAT: 16:9 widescreen, 30 FPS, total duration 4 minutes 28 seconds, photorealistic live-action fantasy film, dreamy vintage 35mm cinema aesthetic.

Create a breathtaking, wordless cinematic fantasy romance about a mysterious mermaid and a lonely castaway who gradually fall in love through shy glances, secret gifts, flowers, seashells, and tender moments. Tell the entire story visually without spoken dialogue, using expressive faces, natural body language, subtle emotions, and poetic underwater imagery.

VISUAL STYLE

Photorealistic live-action cinematography, never cartoonish or animated. Vintage 35mm film texture, fine film grain, soft halation around highlights, gently lifted blacks, pastel colors, soft atmospheric haze, dreamy shallow depth of field, creamy bokeh, realistic skin pores, detailed wet hair, physically believable water reflections, natural underwater light scattering, and smooth cinematic camera movement.

Color palette: turquoise and teal lagoon water, deep navy-blue ocean, warm golden-beige sand and granite, misty pink-lavender skies, vivid purple and magenta flowers, and translucent pink-white mermaid fins. Use soft golden-hour lighting, gentle diffusion, sparkling reflections, and romantic cinematic composition.

CHARACTER A — THE MERMAID

A beautiful adult mermaid with glowing olive-tan skin, long jet-black wet hair, dramatic smoky eye makeup, sharp winged eyeliner, deep berry-brown lips, shimmering cheekbones, and long pointed dark navy-blue acrylic nails. Delicate scale-pattern tattoos and iridescent shimmer decorate her arms and shoulders.

She wears a natural top made of blue-grey seashells and fish-scale pieces. When underwater, her lower body is a powerful fish tail covered in deep blue-black scales, gradually fading into a large translucent pink-white fin that glows softly in sunlight.

Her personality is shy, playful, mischievous, curious, and deeply romantic. She hides behind rocks, peeks above the water, leaves little gifts, watches the man from a distance, and expresses affection through gentle smiles and expressive eyes.

Continuity: Maintain the exact same face, eye makeup, hairstyle, nails, shell top, tattoos, tail colors, and body proportions in every appearance. When she transforms into human form, preserve her identical face, hair, makeup, and upper-body appearance.

CHARACTER B — THE CASTAWAY

A rugged, muscular adult man in his late thirties, with tanned sun-weathered skin, long wet brown hair with lighter sun-streaked strands, a thick full beard, and expressive gentle eyes. He wears a short dark-leaf and natural-fiber loincloth, a black leather strap around his left wrist, and no footwear.

He is curious, lonely, tender, and quietly hopeful. His expressions evolve naturally from confusion and wonder to affection, vulnerability, and love.

Continuity: Preserve the exact same face, beard, hairstyle, physique, clothing, wrist strap, and skin tone throughout the film.

LOCATION

A secluded tropical cove surrounded by enormous weathered granite boulders covered in green moss, pebble-strewn shorelines, soft golden sand, a calm turquoise lagoon, coastal bushes, and a rugged green hillside. Beyond the cove lies a deep navy-blue ocean beneath a misty pink-lavender horizon.

Light sea fog drifts between the rocks. Underwater scenes feature volumetric sunbeams, floating particles, delicate bubbles, realistic underwater caustics, and gently swaying seaweed.

SHOT-BY-SHOT SEQUENCE

SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:10 | The Secret Message

Underwater macro shot with an 85mm cinematic lens look. Against a deep navy-blue background, the mermaid's delicate hands, with long dark navy nails, hold a flat green stone covered in moss. The stone has the naturally carved inscription “I ♥ U”. Tiny bubbles rise around her fingers as the camera slowly pushes toward the message. Soft blue sun rays illuminate the moss and her shimmering skin. Muffled underwater ambience and delicate harp notes.

SHOT 2 — 0:10–0:20 | The Lonely Castaway

Wide establishing shot at eye level. The rugged castaway walks barefoot across warm golden sand between enormous moss-covered boulders, approaching the turquoise water. The misty pink sky reflects across the waves. The camera slowly pushes forward as he pauses and looks around, sensing that someone might be watching him.

SHOT 3 — 0:20–0:30 | A Secret Gift

Low-angle close-up near pebbles and moss. Half concealed behind a granite boulder, the mermaid carefully places a tiny green gift on a moss-covered log. Her long dark nails and delicate scale-pattern tattoos are visible. In the softly blurred background, the castaway's bare legs walk past without noticing her. Natural pebble sounds and gentle waves.

SHOT 4 — 0:30–0:40 | Hidden Glances

Medium over-the-shoulder shot with the castaway's shoulder in the foreground. His bearded profile is sharply focused as he gazes toward the sea. Behind him, the mermaid's forehead and expressive smoky eyes slowly appear above the water beside a boulder. She gives a shy, playful smile. A slow rack focus transfers attention from the man to the mermaid.

SHOT 5 — 0:40–0:50 | Playful Hiding

Low-angle water-level composition. A tiny sandcastle sits in the shallow lagoon. The mermaid hides behind it, revealing only her heavily lined eyes and wet black hair. Her eyes sparkle with mischief as she watches the castaway walking along the distant beach. Soft turquoise ripples move naturally across the foreground.

SHOT 6 — 0:50–1:00 | The Glowing Pearl

Medium shot of the castaway crouching beside another little sandcastle. He discovers a luminous pink-purple pearl and lifts it delicately between two fingers. The pearl casts a subtle rosy reflection across his amazed face. At the right edge of the composition, softly out of focus behind a rock, the mermaid watches his reaction with a secret smile.

SHOT 7 — 1:00–1:20 | Flowers in a Coconut Vase

Dreamy pastel dusk with intimate handheld cinematography. The castaway sits on a weathered rock and carefully cuts the top from a green coconut. Macro close-ups show his strong hands turning it into a natural vase and arranging tiny white and purple wildflowers inside. He gently places the coconut vase on the water. A thin natural fiber string draws it slowly toward the rocks where the mermaid hides. Delicate ripples catch the pink-violet light.

SHOT 8 — 1:20–1:40 | An Offering of Love

Medium shot of the castaway seated beside the turquoise lagoon, holding out a bouquet of vivid purple flowers toward the water. His posture is gentle and hopeful. Cut to an extreme close-up of his emotional eyes, water droplets clinging to his beard, and the textured wet granite beside him. He breathes softly while the flowers move in the sea breeze. Romantic strings begin to swell.

SHOT 9 — 1:40–2:00 | Their First Embrace

Soft pink-lavender color grade, slightly desaturated vintage film texture. The mermaid appears in human form beside the castaway. They stand waist-deep in the shallow water between the giant rocks, facing each other with quiet disbelief and affection. They slowly move closer and embrace, their foreheads touching and eyes closing. The camera makes a graceful, slow arc around them as their wet hair moves in the breeze and the water ripples around their bodies.

SHOT 10 — 2:00–2:20 | Roses Beneath the Waves

Begin underwater in deep blue light. The mermaid swims gracefully toward the camera, extending both hands to offer a bouquet of vivid purple roses with long green stems. Her black hair floats weightlessly around her face, and tiny bubbles rise past her shoulders.

Transition smoothly to sunset above the water. The mermaid and castaway stand chest-deep in the calm sea, faces close, exchanging tender smiles. Purple roses float between them as the pink-violet sky shimmers across the water. The music becomes warmer and more romantic.

SHOT 11 — 2:20–2:50 | The Sea King's Anger

Sudden emotional cutaway to a darker blue-teal underwater environment. A powerful, bearded adult sea king with grey-blond floating hair and purple-blue scaled armor roars furiously underwater. Bubbles stream from his mouth as the camera pushes into an extreme close-up of his intense, angry eyes. Add a deep orchestral drum swell and low rumbling bass.

Cut to an older sea-woman with a braided updo and intricate arm markings. She embraces a distressed dark-haired figure with sorrow and concern. Their expressions communicate fear, grief, and a mysterious family conflict without dialogue. End with a wall of green seaweed swaying slowly across the entire frame, creating a natural underwater transition.

SHOT 12 — 2:50–3:10 | A Leap of Faith

Return to the hidden cove with warm golden light and gentle romantic music. The castaway stands on a lush green rocky hillside, with a beautiful wreath of purple flowers resting on a nearby boulder. He looks toward the sea with quiet determination, then runs a short distance and dives gracefully from a golden rock into the turquoise water.

Underwater, the mermaid waits below the surface, holding red and purple flowers. Sun rays illuminate her shell top and blue-black scales as she turns toward him.

SHOT 13 — 3:10–3:30 | The Shell and the Crown

Close-up of the castaway kneeling on wet golden sand, holding a large spiral conch shell. He slowly tips it, allowing a delicate stream of sand and water to spill onto the beach. His hands are realistic, weathered, and detailed.

Transition to a cinematic split-level shot, with half the camera above water and half below. The mermaid slowly rises through the turquoise surface wearing a vivid purple flower crown. Her face glows in the sunlight while the underwater portion reveals her deep blue-black tail and translucent pink-white fin. Sparkling highlights dance across the waterline.

SHOT 14 — 3:30–3:50 | The Mermaid's Dance

Underwater wide shot with strong blue sun rays. Wearing the purple flower crown, the mermaid performs an elegant, graceful dance. Her arms flow like sea currents, her long black hair floats around her, and her expression is warm and joyful. Purple and pink petals drift around her.

She slowly turns away and swims into the deeper blue water. Her powerful tail moves naturally, and the large translucent pink-white fin sweeps across the camera, briefly filling the frame with shimmering color. Follow her with a smooth floating camera movement.

SHOT 15 — 3:50–4:10 | Another Little Gift

Back on the beach, a rear-view medium shot shows the castaway reaching into lush green coastal bushes and picking up an orange shell. Warm sunlight illuminates his wet brown hair and muscular shoulders.

Cut to the mermaid lying peacefully on wet golden sand, her back toward the camera. Beside her is a carefully arranged collection of small gifts: a little bamboo stick, colorful seashells, purple flowers, and natural treasures. Golden light falls softly across her shoulders and wet black hair. The scene feels intimate, mysterious, and full of unspoken affection.

SHOT 16 — 4:10–4:28 | Footprints and Farewell

Underwater point-of-view shot looking toward rippled golden sand beneath the clear turquoise sea. Dark footprints are visible in the sand, leading toward the shallows. The castaway's arm slowly enters the frame as sunlight flickers over his skin and the sandy bottom.

The camera gradually rises toward the bright surface light. Tiny particles drift upward, the underwater ambience softens, and the orchestral music reaches a gentle emotional resolution. Fade slowly to black during the final seconds.

AUDIO DESIGN

Absolutely no spoken dialogue, narration, or subtitles. Use an original soft romantic orchestral score featuring delicate harp, warm strings, gentle piano, and subtle chimes. Let the score build gradually with the relationship.

Layer realistic environmental sounds throughout: rolling waves, water lapping against sand, distant seabirds, wind moving through coastal bushes, subtle splashes, and muffled underwater ambience with soft bubbles. During the sea king sequence, introduce a deep drum swell and low rumbling bass. Finish with warm strings, a gentle piano resolution, and a slow audio fade.

STRICT CONTINUITY REQUIREMENTS

Maintain the same recognizable faces, hairstyles, body types, skin tones, outfits, tattoos, nail colors, tail design, and flower colors throughout every shot. Preserve the exact geography and appearance of the tropical cove, including the same moss-covered boulders, shoreline, lagoon, and hillside.

Use physically realistic water, natural hair movement, believable body mechanics, anatomically correct hands, consistent lighting direction, and smooth transitions. Keep the mermaid's fish tail visible in underwater scenes and use her human form only for the designated romantic embrace and above-water human-form scenes. Preserve the story's gentle, mysterious, romantic atmosphere.

NEGATIVE PROMPT

No cartoon, anime, illustration, video-game graphics, or artificial CGI-cartoon appearance. No text overlays except the naturally carved “I ♥ U” on the stone. No subtitles, watermarks, logos, modern objects, buildings, boats, or unrelated characters. No extra fingers, missing limbs, duplicated body parts, malformed hands, distorted faces, changing identities, inconsistent costumes, changing hair colors, incorrect tail colors, flickering, jitter, unnatural motion, sudden unwanted jump cuts, warped anatomy, plastic skin, oversaturated colors, harsh artificial lighting, overexposed highlights, low resolution, or blurry main subjects.

FINAL RESULT: A visually coherent, photorealistic, dreamy vintage fantasy romance in which every gift, glance, flower, and underwater movement tells the story of two lonely souls discovering love without saying a single word.

Investigators say Mogambi allegedly used stolen personal details of U.S. citizens to enrol fake students in online universities, secure federal student loans, forge refund checks and transfer thousands of dollars to bank accounts in Kenya.

The institutions reportedly linked to the scheme include Grand Canyon University, Colorado Technical University and American Public University.

The investigation gained momentum after an acquaintance he allegedly offered $2,000 weekly to help process fraudulent checks reported him to police.

A subsequent investigation uncovered forged checks, financial records and academic loan documents linking him to the operation.

If convicted, Mogambi faces up to 20 years in prison under Nebraska law. His immigration status could also be affected by the outcome of the case.

text:
FAULTLINE | GLOBAL BRIEF
30 OCTOBER 2026

THE COST OF DEPENDENCE

1. G20 | INDIA AT THE TABLE, QUAD ON THE SIDELINES

G20 foreign ministers meet in Atlanta on October 30–31, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is attending. Energy security, freedom of navigation and supply chains are among the priorities.

Russia's participation remains disputed. Rubio says Russian officials will attend, while Moscow says Washington has not confirmed its delegation list. A Quad foreign ministers' meeting is also scheduled on the sidelines. China's attendance has not been established.

THE CONVERSATION IS ABOUT MORE THAN TRADE.

Energy routes, supply chains and maritime security are now central to economic diplomacy. For India, the G20 and Quad meetings offer two different platforms to engage with major powers on overlapping strategic interests.

2. UKRAINE | THE PRICE OF SAYING NO

A Wall Street Journal investigation reports that Washington asked Kyiv around six times to stop attacking Russian oil refineries. Ukraine paused for approximately three days before resuming strikes on October 15, hitting the Ryazan refinery.

The WSJ reports that analysts estimate the strikes have taken out 40–50% of Russia's refining capacity.
Zelenskyy says Washington warned that intelligence sharing could be cut. Trump says intelligence sharing has not stopped, while US administration officials deny that threats were made.

KYIV'S LEVERAGE COMES WITH A COST.

Ukraine has demonstrated its ability to put significant pressure on Russia's energy infrastructure, but it also depends heavily on American intelligence and military support, including air-defence capabilities.

How far can Kyiv use its leverage against Moscow without risking the support it needs from Washington?

3. US–IRAN | ONE LETTER, TWO INTERPRETATIONS

Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency reports that Tehran received a letter from US Vice-President JD Vance, addressed to security official Mohsen Rezaei. The Wall Street Journal and New York Times report that the letter was intended to reopen negotiations.

President Trump said the message concerned medical supplies and that he had approved Vance sending it.
Iran has not responded. Tasnim reports that Tehran insists its seven conditions be met and considers any position contradicting them unacceptable.

Separately, reports say Trump is weighing a possible week-long military campaign after the November 3 US midterm elections.

THE DIPLOMATIC CHANNEL HAS NOT CLOSED. THE MILITARY OPTION HAS NOT DISAPPEARED.

The letter matters because it comes amid continued disagreement over the terms of any settlement. Communication is taking place, but there is little evidence yet of common ground.

4. AI MARKETS | THE MARKET WANTS PROOF

In Thursday's US session, October 29, Alphabet shares fell 12.64%, wiping out roughly $450–500 billion in market value. The decline followed concerns over its revenue performance and approximately $9 billion in negative free cash flow.

Intel fell sharply after hours, with losses varying between approximately 17% and 23% depending on the reporting time. Amazon fell around 7% after hours.
Asian markets reacted on Friday, October 30. South Korea's KOSPI fell around 5%, while Japan's Nikkei declined nearly 3%.

INVESTORS SPENT TWO YEARS REWARDING AI SPENDING. NOW THEY WANT TO SEE THE RETURNS.

The concern is not whether companies are investing enough in AI. It is whether those investments can generate revenue at the scale markets have already priced in.

5. SOUTH KOREA | THE CHIP ADVANTAGE HAS A COST

A Reuters poll of nine economists forecasts South Korean exports rising 93.2% year-on-year in October, compared with 83.7% growth in September. The forecast points to the strongest growth since 1974, driven largely by semiconductor demand and higher memory-chip prices.

Official October trade figures are due on November 1.
Calendar-adjusted exports rose 65.9% in the first 20 days of October.

BOOMING EXPORTS, A FALLING MARKET.

South Korea's semiconductor industry is benefiting from the AI investment cycle. But the same dependence creates vulnerability. Kelvin Lam of Pantheon Macroeconomics warns that the economy is highly exposed because growth is being driven so heavily by semiconductors.

The KOSPI was on track for a fall of about 17% in October as of Friday trading.
A booming export sector and a sharply falling stock market are unfolding in the same month, both tell part of the story.

THE DAY'S TAKE

Ukraine's dependence on US intelligence, Iran's exposure to sanctions and South Korea's reliance on semiconductor demand point to different versions of the same dilemma.
Countries can build leverage through what others need, but that leverage can become a weakness when they depend on someone else's support.

The question isn't who is strongest. It's who can afford to say no.

 FAULTLINE | Global Pressure Points

Based on reporting available on 30 October 2026. Claims, estimates and forecasts are attributed. Analysis represents FAULTLINE's interpretation.

text:
You crooks refuse to follow The California Constitution
or use the SAVE program to aid in cleaning the voter rolls.
You're a fraud & need removed from your title.The SAVE program most commonly refers to the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system run by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). It is an online verification service that registered federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local government agencies use to check an individual’s immigration status or U.S. citizenship status.

Original purpose and recent expansion
SAVE began in the 1980s as a tool primarily for agencies to verify immigration status when people apply for public benefits or licenses (examples include certain welfare programs, driver’s licenses, or similar).
It has offered limited voter-related verification services since around 2005.
In 2025, under the Trump administration (following Executive Order 14248 on election integrity), USCIS significantly expanded and optimized it. Changes included integrating Social Security Administration (SSA) data, allowing bulk uploads of records, accepting queries using the last four digits of a Social Security number (instead of requiring a full SSN or DHS alien number in all cases), and making the service free for state and local agencies. The explicit goal of the overhaul was to help election officials verify citizenship for voter registration and voter-list maintenance.

Dozens of states and election agencies have entered (or are in the process of entering) memoranda of agreement to use it for voter verification. USCIS reports large volumes of queries—tens of millions related to voter checks.

How it works
Agencies submit identifying information (name, date of birth, and an enumerator such as an SSN or A-number). SAVE queries underlying federal records held by DHS, SSA, the Department of State, and others and returns a point-in-time response indicating citizenship or immigration status if the data is retrievable. 

It is not a comprehensive citizenship database itself, and it does not decide whether someone is eligible to register or vote—the requesting agency makes that determination under applicable law. Non-citizen responses or inconclusive results typically require additional verification steps, notice to the individual, and an opportunity to present proof of citizenship. It cannot always confirm citizenship for certain naturalized or acquired citizens if relevant records are missing or outdated.

Controversies and reliability
Critics (including voting-rights groups and some election officials) have raised concerns about accuracy, false positives that flag U.S. citizens (especially naturalized citizens or those with name changes), privacy implications of linking SSA and other data, and the administrative burden of resolving inconclusive matches. Reported error rates in some state or county reviews have been notable. Supporters view the expanded tool as a practical way to help enforce the federal prohibition on noncitizen voting. A federal court initially blocked aspects of the 2025 expansion on privacy and risk-of-disenfranchisement grounds; the Supreme Court later allowed the changes to proceed via an emergency order in September 2026.

Note on the related SAVE America Act: This is separate legislation (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, sometimes branded SAVE America Act). It is a proposed federal bill (passed by the House in 2026 but not enacted as of the latest available information) that would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and photo ID to vote. Versions of the bill reference or encourage use of the SAVE system for citizenship checks. It is not the same as the USCIS SAVE program.

text:
Kevin Costner and Christine married in 2004. For 18 years they built a life and raised 3 children inside a house he had bought in 1988, long before she ever crossed its threshold. When she filed in May 2023, the prenup that had once felt like a formality turned into the wall between them. It handed her $100,000 on the wedding day, another $100,000 on the first anniversary and $1,000,000 the moment the papers were filed. It also gave her 30 days to leave the house that had never been hers. A judge had to order her out. Money may talk, but in that courtroom it also whispered that even love can come with an eviction notice.

She asked for $248,000 a month in child support and, in the same breath, said she did not know how she would afford groceries. He offered roughly $51,000. A temporary order set $129,755. She moved into a $40,000-a-month rental and still said the children needed more. That summer she was photographed in Hawaii with a family friend, Josh Connor. By the time the final number arrived in September 2023, $63,209 a month...the public had already begun counting the candles on both sides of the table. She later married him. Blood is thicker than water, yet the camera rarely lies about who shares the sunlight after the papers are signed.

In court Costner arrived and said, "We’re talking about somebody I love on the other side." Listen closely and you will hear her claim that something essential lives in the children’s DNA.… something the ledger cannot measure. On one side of the scales sit 18 years, 3 children and a husband earning over $1,000,000 a month on Yellowstone. On the other sit a signed prenup and their oldest son driving a 15-year-old truck. A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush, but when the bush is Hollywood and the hand once held a family, the math grows cruel.

Was $63,209 a month for 3 children fair, or did the ask outrun the need? You cannot pour new wine into old wineskins and you cannot measure a childhood solely by the rent. The house that love once filled now stands as proof that some contracts outlast the people who sign them. What remains is the oldest question of all: when the fortune is vast and the children are small, who decides what is enough and who pays the price when love and the ledger finally part ways?

There's another surgery I'm preparing for after my gallbladder surgery. This one is for my heart.

The date hasn't been set yet. It depends on how quickly I can lose the extra weight without my heart getting so bad that the doctors can't wait any longer.

Personally, I'm hoping it can wait until after summer 2027. That would give me time to recover before the fall semester, when I plan to enter a dual master's program.

After recovery, there are so many things I want to do that I've been missing out on because of my heart.

I've been thinking about starting a YouTube channel to document all the fun things I finally get to experience.

I want to visit Hawaii and Alaska so I can say I've been to all 50 states. Internationally, Brazil, Japan, and possibly England are on my list. I'd also love to scout locations for my books while I'm traveling.

And one of my nurses has offered to teach me pickleball! 😂

Maybe I'll even include some of the people I've met online in my YouTube adventures if I happen to visit their areas. It could be fun to finally meet some of the people I've spent so much time chatting with.

I've spent a lot of time thinking about what I can't do because of my heart. I'm looking forward to finding out what I can do after surgery and recovery.

I'd love some ideas for adventures, activities, and experiences to add to my list!

text:
His manager had pulled him aside and asked whether the job was becoming too much.

Dad had spent six weeks learning where everything went. Now someone else was unloading his cart while he stood beside it.

“I applied for a job,” he said. “You’ve made it sound like you dropped me off for the morning.”

I said I was worried about him.

“I know. But you ask me if I’m tired before you ask me how my day went.”

I didn’t have much to say to that.

Then he told me about work.

He had breakfast with Joan after the Tuesday delivery. A college student named Marcus had taught him how to swap shifts on his phone. They’d asked him to train the next person because he actually checked the dates instead of pushing new stock in front.

I hadn’t known any of that.

I offered to call his manager and explain.

“No,” he said. “I’ll talk to him.”

So I apologized to Dad and left it there.

This week, I went shopping after his shift.

On Friday, I called to invite him for Sunday dinner.

He couldn’t come. Joan needed the day off for her grandson’s birthday, and he’d offered to cover.

For a second, I wanted to tell him they shouldn’t be relying on him so much.

“Would Monday work?” I asked.

“Monday’s good. Don’t buy bread. I’ll bring some.”

Then he added, “And stop buying those little bags of rice. The big one’s on sale. You’re getting robbed.”
